ui.data.title: What the data says about {hero}
ui.data.desc: What players do, compared with the other heroes at the same net worth or at equal game state. These are not instructions: "How to play" crosses them with the kit and creators.
ui.data.lane_detail: {kd} kill per 10 min · {souls} souls for the duo around {min} min
ui.data.fights_desc: After the lane: kills minus deaths of his whole team per 10 min, gap to the other heroes at the same net worth. The coloured band is his spike window. Markers sit at the hero's median net worth at their minute; the bar covers half of the games.
ui.data.timing_title: By minute, at equal game state
ui.data.timing_desc: Same soul lead or deficit for his team, same share of its souls: what he adds to or takes from his team's fights, per 10 min.
ui.data.lane_items_desc: Tier 1 items that never upgrade: bought for the lane, sold when slots run out. Effect on the lane when he buys them before his lane ends, compared with the same hero without the item against the same opponent.
ui.data.items_desc: Team fights in the 5 min after the purchase against the 5 min before, beyond this hero's usual rise at the same minute: what the item changes, not who buys it. Only items bought in at least 10% of games are listed; clear effects are coloured.
ui.data.farm_desc: Where his souls come from, by phase, compared with the average hero.
ui.data.keys_desc: What separates his won games from his lost games at equal net worth, clearly more than for other heroes (30 to 40 min games). To be explained with the kit.
ui.data.keys_none: No resource stands out clearly: his impact comes from timing and team play.
ui.tl.power_note: Measured after the laning phase, over {n} ranked games.
ui.data.lane_cut_tip: The laning phase is not counted: the dotted line marks their average net worth at the end of their lane. Points to its left come from players still below that net worth after their lane.
ui.data.how.f1: Source: {n} ranked games from {from} to {to}, from the public deadlock-api data lake (each player's statistics, recorded during the game).
ui.data.how.f2: The laning phase is removed. For each player it ends when the first guardian of their lane falls (around {min} min on average for this hero). Only the fights that follow count, hence the hatched area on the left of the chart.
ui.data.how.f3: Each death after the lane counts for their team: +1 when an enemy dies, −1 when an ally dies, whoever the killer is. A tank who kills nobody but wins fights is therefore measured properly.
ui.data.how.f4: Each death is placed at the net worth they have at that second, in 2,500-soul brackets. The time they spend in each bracket is counted too.
ui.data.how.f5: In each bracket: the sum of the +1s and −1s, divided by the time spent, scaled to 10 min. This gives their team's net kills per 10 min at that net worth.
ui.data.how.f6: The exact same computation is done for all heroes together: that is the reference. The curve shows the gap between the two, which is why the reference is a flat line at 0. Without the gap, everyone would rise with money, because a rich player is often on the winning team.
ui.data.how.f7: Values are smoothed with the neighbouring brackets. A bracket is only shown with enough playing time; otherwise the curve stops.
ui.data.how.f8: The spike compares the curve with their own average: the band covers the brackets that reach at least 60% of their peak. A spike can therefore sit below 0: it is their best moment, not necessarily better than other heroes.
ui.data.how.fex: Example, between {a} and {b} souls: {hero}'s team gets {h} net kills per 10 min, another hero's team at the same net worth {r}. The gap, {d}, is the point plotted there.
ui.data.how.t1: The same deaths as above (after the lane, +1 enemy, −1 ally), but placed by game minute instead of net worth.
ui.data.how.t2: Each moment is also classified by game state: their team's soul lead or deficit (5 levels, from "more than 10% behind" to "more than 10% ahead") and their share of the team's souls (below 90%, normal, above 110% of their allies' average).
ui.data.how.t3: In each cell, their net kills per 10 min are compared with other heroes in the same cell, then the cells are averaged, weighted by time played.
ui.data.how.t4: So a hero often played in games already won gets no advantage: they are always compared in the same situation. The "Being fed" tile uses the same cells: high share of souls against normal.
ui.data.how.l1: Tier 1 items that are part of no other item's recipe: bought for the lane and sold later.
ui.data.how.l2: Their lanes where they bought the item before the lane ended are compared with their lanes without it, against the same enemy hero, then averaged over all opponents.
ui.data.how.l3: Measured at lane end: soul gap between their duo and the enemy duo, and lane kills minus deaths per 10 min.
ui.data.how.l4: The margin of error is two standard errors. If it crosses zero, we cannot say the item changes anything: the row is greyed out.
ui.data.how.l5: "Mostly bought against": how many times more often they buy it against this hero than on average. It says what players fear, not that it works.
ui.data.how.i1: For each purchase made between 5 min and 5 min before the end: their team's net kills in the next 5 min minus the previous 5 min.
ui.data.how.i2: The hero's usual change at the same minute (any purchase) is removed: what remains is what this item adds. The result is scaled to 10 min.
ui.data.how.i3: Win rate is never used: an item bought while already winning would look strong without being so.
ui.data.how.i4: Only items bought in at least 10% of their games are listed. ✓ = effect at least 2.5 standard errors above zero; the others are greyed out.
ui.data.how.r1: Player statistics are recorded every 3 min until 15 min, then every 5 min. The souls earned between two records are used.
ui.data.how.r2: Sources given by the game: lane troopers (with their orbs), jungle (neutral camps), kills and assists, objectives (guardians, boss, team bonus). Rift, urn and crates are counted apart, outside the bars.
ui.data.how.r3: Phases: their lane (until the first guardian of their lane), then until 20 min, 20 to 30 min and after 30 min. "Average" = all heroes over the same phase.
ui.data.how.k1: Blind search: about ten end-of-game statistics (kills, deaths, assists, soul sources, healing, damage…) and the permanent bonuses of their abilities are tested, assuming nothing about the kit.
ui.data.how.k2: For each one, their 30-40 min games are split in two halves (above or below the median), at equal net worth in 5,000-soul brackets, and the win rate gap is measured.
ui.data.how.k3: This gap is compared with other heroes' gap for the same statistic (for an ability bonus, with the gap of their own kills). What matters is the excess.
ui.data.how.k4: A resource only shows if the excess is above 3 points and solid (at least 2.5 standard errors). It is a lead to explain with the kit, not an instruction.
ui.data.tip_up: With them, their team gets {v} more net kills (kills − deaths) per 10 min than with another hero at this net worth.
ui.data.tip_down: With them, their team gets {v} fewer net kills (kills − deaths) per 10 min than with another hero at this net worth.
ui.data.tip_even: As much weight as another hero at this net worth.
ui.data.tip_none: Not enough games here to measure.
ui.data.obj_tip: Spawns at {min} min. At that minute they usually have {nw} souls (half of the games between {lo} and {hi}).
ui.data.lg_ref: 0 = another hero at the same net worth
ui.data.lg_obj: spawn minute, placed at their median net worth
ui.data.lg_usual: other heroes (or their kills, for a bonus)
ui.data.tip_clear: The margin of error does not reach zero: the effect is clear.
ui.data.tip_unclear: The margin of error crosses zero: no clear difference.
ui.data.lane_item_tip: Compared with the same hero without the item, against the same lane opponent.
ui.data.item_tip: Their team's net kills per 10 min, 5 min after the purchase against 5 min before, beyond their usual rise at the same minute.
ui.data.timing_tip: Compared with other heroes, at the same team soul lead or deficit.
ui.data.farm_tip: Share of their souls by source; in brackets, the average of all heroes.
ui.data.key_tip: Win rate gap between their games where this value is high and those where it is low, at equal net worth.
ui.data.help_wr: Share of their games won. On its own, this says neither when nor how they win.
ui.data.help_lane: Kills minus deaths of their duo per 10 min of lane, and soul gap with the enemy duo when the first guardian of their lane falls.
ui.data.help_spike: Net worth window where they weigh most on fights, compared with their own average. The minutes are when they usually reach that net worth.
ui.data.help_best: Period where they add the most to fights at an equal game state (same team soul lead, same share of souls).
ui.data.help_fed: What a soul lead (110% of their allies' souls) gives them beyond an average hero, in their team's net kills per 10 min.
ui.data.help_antiheal: They heal themselves at least 1.5 times more than the average hero: anti-heal becomes useful against them from this net worth.
ui.data.key_line: {gap} win-rate points when it is high, against {usual} for {ref}

ui.ctr.title: Counter items
ui.ctr.desc: Situational items {author} buys clearly more often against some heroes (purchase rate against that hero vs their overall rate). Computed on their games since {date}.
ui.pos.1: Takes the most souls on the team and wins the late game. Until ~15 min, mostly PvE (waves, side lane, camps). Their target in fights: the enemy carry.
ui.pos.2: Lots of souls, but a much earlier power spike (≈ 8 to 15 min): gank, take fights, force objectives. AFK farming at 12 min wastes that spike.
ui.pos.3: Average farm. Engages first, soaks damage and survives while the carries deal damage. After the lanes: split push and objectives.
ui.pos.4: Low farm. Leaves their lane to be where the fights are: ganks, picks, scouting. Farms on the move.
ui.pos.5: Low farm. Weakens enemies and buys team items (crowd control, hexes) to shut down the enemy carry.
ui.pos.6: The fewest souls. Heals, protects and saves the carries at the right time. Rule #1: don't die.
ui.pos.note: Positions 1 to 6 = farm priority in the community meta (the game enforces no role). P1 takes the most souls, P6 the fewest. Source: Steam guide “Roles Explained”.

ui.lane.general: · this hero also wins the lane against most heroes ({n} souls on average)
ui.vs.beaten_desc: Gap to the expected result (each hero's overall strength is removed). {hero} wins {base}% of games on average.
ui.vs.small: Small gaps: at high level, no hero really counters {hero}. Play on their weaknesses rather than on the pick.
